title: Geometric fibres detect exactness in the constructible adic heart
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and use the constructible heart $\Sh_c(Y,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-constructible-heart] of the rationalized/common-finite-coefficient-stage adic category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. For a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$, let $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ denote the geometric coefficient fibre, computed by derived pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the point-fibre functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules]. These fibre functors are exact and jointly conservative on the constructible heart. Thus a morphism in this heart is zero if all its geometric fibres are zero, and a short complex [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] is short exact if and only if the corresponding sequence of finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces is short exact at every geometric point. The same assertions hold for constructible Weil sheaves [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] after forgetting the Weil structure. Exactness of locally constructible adic sheaf sequences on a locally finite-type $k_0$-scheme can be checked on a covering by separated finite-type open subschemes. This assertion concerns constructible adic coefficient fibres, not arbitrary sheaves on the pro-etale topos.

source.place: §6.8, Proposition 6.8.4, Corollary 6.8.5, Lemma 6.8.7 and Proposition 6.8.14; finite etale-level detection is Stacks Tag 03PU, etale-cohomology-theorem-exactness-stalks. Applied to the constructible heart, with rationalization and common-stage coefficients as specified in the statement.

proof.text: Work first at a finite coefficient field $E$. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is of finite type over a field. A $k$-linear point $y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ is a section of the separated structure morphism, so is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. Every map $s\to Y$ in the statement has this form up to an automorphism of $s$: its map on the base field is a self-embedding of $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, hence an automorphism, because it permutes each finite subfield. A scheme automorphism is itself a locally closed immersion. Thus it suffices for exactness to treat locally closed immersions.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 (closed immersions); elementary reduction to closed k-points

proof.text: For a locally closed immersion $a:S\to Y$, [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison] identifies completed integral pullback with ordinary exact inverse image and says it preserves integral constructibility. Since every scheme here is of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian and finite-dimensional with $\ell$ invertible, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] says that the integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] used by the constructible heart is exactly the category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], with the same completed ring sheaf; the two raw rationalizations therefore coincide. Its exact rationalization is [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. It preserves each half of the rational standard pair: represent an object in that half by an integral object in the corresponding half, as in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], and apply the exact integral inverse image. Consequently $La^*$ is $t$-exact. In particular this applies to $y:s\to Y$ and to every stratum immersion used below.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15: inverse image under locally closed immersions is naive inverse image

proof.text: At $s$, [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] gives $H^r\Gamma(s,K)=\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^rK)$ at the integral stage. Tensoring these module complexes with $E$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Hence the point-fibre functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] preserves both halves of the rational standard pair. Its values are bounded complexes with finite-dimensional cohomology by [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness]. Together with Step 2 this makes $\operatorname{Fib}_sLy^*$ a triangulated, $t$-exact functor whose restriction to the heart takes values in finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces. The short-exact/triangle correspondence in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], applied before and after this functor, proves that this restriction is exact.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; evaluation on Spec k and passage to E

proof.text: Pass to $\Qlb$ using the actual common-stage category, rather than a discrete constant-coefficient category. By [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], every finite diagram of objects, arrows and asserted equalities has a representative at a common finite field. By [prop-constructible-truncations], truncations commute with finite scalar extension and with the coefficient transitions. Thus heart objects may be replaced by $H^0$ of their representatives; kernels and cokernels are obtained from cones by the formulas in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], and are represented at the same stage. The immersion pullbacks of Step 2 preserve the two halves stagewise. The point-fibre scalar comparisons of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] make Step 3 independent of representatives. Finally [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension] identifies its degree-zero value with the finite-stage vector space tensored with $\Qlb$. The short-exact/triangle criterion again proves exactness of every fibre functor on $\Sh_c(Y,\Qlb)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and the common-stage coefficient construction

proof.text: To prove zero-object detection, take $F\in\Sh_c(Y,\Qlb)$ represented by a heart object $F_E$ over one finite field, as in Step 4. Use the equivalence $J_Y$ of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]; its source category is the raw rationalization of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], which is the category $D^b_c(Y,E)$ containing $F_E$ by the identification of integral categories in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] (Step 2). Its coefficient ring is the sheaf of continuous $E$-valued functions, and it is induced by derived extension of scalars from the completed integral ring, not by extension to a discrete constant sheaf. That extension is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-scalar-exact]; it therefore preserves cohomology by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology]. The definitions of the rational standard pair imply that $J_Y$ sends both halves into the ambient standard halves. Thus $J_Y(F_E)$ is a sheaf in degree zero. The same realization lemma says its cohomology is stratified locally free of finite rank over the continuous coefficient sheaf. The essential-image assertion of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] identifies these locally free sheaves with the lisse subcategory of the rational heart, so $F_E$ restricts to a lisse $E$-sheaf on each stratum. The pullback comparisons in that lemma identify these restrictions with $J_S(La^*F_E)$.

Refine the partition of Step 5 to a good stratification using [lem-sfb-noetherian-good-stratification-refinement]; the realized sheaf $L_S=J_S(La^*F_E)$ is still lisse on each refined stratum $S$, by restriction. Give $S$ its reduced subscheme structure: it is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme whose underlying space is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open] its connected components $C$ are finitely many and open, so they form a finite Zariski open covering of $S$ by nonempty connected separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Each $C$ has a $k$-point $x:s\to C$: a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C$ has $A\ne0$ finitely generated over $k$, and a maximal ideal of $A$ has residue field $k$ by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](1). Its composite $s\to C\to S\to Y$ is a point tested by the hypothesis. By [det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank] the rank loci of the lisse sheaf $L_S|_C$ are open and closed in $C$; since $C$ is connected, $L_S|_C$ has one constant rank $r_C\ge0$, i.e. it is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $E_C^{\oplus r_C}$.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3 and Definition 6.8.6 (lisse = locally free of finite rank on strata); Stacks 04MF and the Nullstellensatz; reviewer repair of the point-fibre argument

proof.text: Suppose every displayed fibre of $F$ is zero; fix a component $C$ of a stratum $S$ and its $k$-point $x$ from Step 6, and let $b:C\to Y$ be the immersion. By Steps 3 and 4, $\operatorname{Fib}_sLx^*Lb^*F_E$ is an $E$-vector space in degree zero whose extension to $\Qlb$ is the fibre of $F$ at $bx$, hence zero; so it is zero, since scalar extension of a nonzero vector space contains an extended basis vector. By [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] for $x:s\to C$ (its comparisons hold for all scheme morphisms of finite-type $k$-schemes), this fibre is the sections at $s$ of the ordinary pullback $x^*L_C$ of the realized lisse sheaf $L_C=L_S|_C$, which the pullback comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] identify with $J_C(Lb^*F_E)$; and $x^*$ sends a local basis to a local basis, so $x^*L_C$ is pro-etale locally $E_s^{\oplus r_C}$. Take a nonempty affine member $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of such a trivializing covering of $s$. The one-point space $s$ is w-local with extremally disconnected component space and $k$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-w-local, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and $k\to B$ is faithfully flat weakly etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-geometric-criterion] gives a retraction, i.e. a section $\sigma:s\to W$ over $s$. The sections of $x^*L_C$ at $s$ equal those of its restriction to $W$ at $(s,\sigma)$, namely $E_s(s)^{\oplus r_C}=E^{\oplus r_C}$, using the continuous-function description of the coefficient ring in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Hence $r_C=0$, so $L_C$ is pro-etale locally zero and therefore zero. The components cover $S$, so [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism], applied to $0\to L_S$, gives $L_S=0$. Since $J_S$ is an equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], $La^*F_E=0$, i.e. $F_E|_S=0$ for every stratum.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3 (lisse E-sheaves locally free of finite rank) and Proposition 6.8.14(2); evaluation at the weakly contractible point Spec k; reviewer repair

proof.text: A finite good stratification has a stratum open in the union of the remaining strata: choose one maximal in the closure order; its complement is a finite union of closed strata-closures. Remove such an open stratum successively. At each stage [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] gives $j_!j^*F_E\to F_E\to i_*i^*F_E\to$. The restriction to the removed stratum is zero by Step 7, and the restriction to its closed complement is zero by induction on the number of strata. Thus both outer terms are zero, and $F_E=0$. On the empty scheme the empty covering and the sheaf axiom force every module to be zero; this is the zero-stratum base case. Therefore $F=0$. This proves joint zero-object detection without any assertion about arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Definition 6.8.6, finite stratification devissage using open-closed triangles

proof.text: For a morphism $u:F\to G$, exactness of the fibres (Step 4) identifies the fibres of $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker}u$ with the corresponding vector-space kernel and cokernel, by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a). If every fibre map is an isomorphism, both objects have zero fibres, hence are zero by Step 8, so $u$ is an isomorphism. This is joint conservativity. If every fibre map is zero, [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](b) gives zero fibres of $\operatorname{im}u$; Step 8 gives $\operatorname{im}u=0$, hence $u=0$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.7; elementary kernel, cokernel and image argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jointly-reflect-short-exact] to the abelian constructible heart and the family of geometric coefficient fibres. Step 4 supplies preservation of finite limits and colimits and zero morphisms (exact additive functors), and Step 9 supplies joint reflection of isomorphisms. Its conclusion is precisely the claimed equivalence between short exactness in the heart and short exactness of every sequence of finite-dimensional fibres.

source.place: Finite-stage stalk criterion (Stacks Tag 03PU), transferred to the constructible heart

proof.text: For Weil sheaves, Frobenius pullback preserves the standard truncations by [prop-constructible-truncations], and is an autoequivalence. In the fixed-pair description [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], the kernel of an equivariant arrow inherits its structure isomorphism by the kernel universal property, applied to the commuting square; its inverse is induced by the inverse Frobenius structures. The identical cokernel construction gives a cokernel fixed pair. Thus kernels and cokernels are created in the underlying heart, and the faithful forgetful functor is exact and reflects exactness and zero arrows. Steps 4, 9 and 10 therefore give all the stated Weil-sheaf assertions after forgetting structure.

source.place: Weil structures: fixed pairs; Proposition 6.8.14 and ordinary heart operations

proof.text: Finally, on a locally finite-type $k_0$-scheme use separated finite-type affine opens. Restriction to an open is exact by the immersion argument of Step 2, locally at a finite coefficient stage. For a short complex form its kernel at the left, its middle homology and its cokernel at the right; [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] says these restrict to the corresponding three defects. A locally constructible defect which restricts to zero on the covering is zero: it suffices to test this on every affine open $V$ of finite type, which is separated, so that $V$ is covered by its finitely many separated finite-type intersections with members of the covering; realize the defect on $V$ by Step 5 as a continuous-coefficient module sheaf and apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to its zero map. A finite subcover suffices there, so all required diagrams and their zero restrictions can be taken at a common finite coefficient stage by [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Hence the three defects vanish globally exactly when they vanish on the covering. This proves the locality clause; no global finite coefficient field on a non-quasi-compact scheme is required.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 and sheaf locality for open covers
